newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's Rocard sees chaos if euro calendar slips.
newsitem.headline: France's Rocard sees chaos if euro calendar slips.

text.p: Former French Socialist prime minister Michel Rocard warned European Union nations on Sunday to stick to the planned calendar for introducing a single currency, or risk "the end of Europe."
He also said EU countries should allow flexibility in interpreting the Maastricht Treaty criteria for qualifying for the euro currency from 1999.
"The dispute over the calendar is about whether or not we carry out an international treaty," Rocard told Radio J in an interview.

"If we question this international treaty, there is no hope of replacing it. Any reopening of talks about the calendar means giving up, failure, a strategic void, the end of 40 to 50 years of European diplomacy," he said.

"It's the end of Europe and I would then advise my children and grandchildren to apply for Australian passports," said Rocard, who was prime minister to late president Francois Mitterrand in 1988-1991.
"As long as we don't have the single currency, the market can explode again into a monetary crisis," he said. "It means Europe would become a place of rivalry, possibly war. It's frightening."

He also said, "We have to combat some mythological or symbolic excesses" about a Maastricht requirement for nations to limit their 1997 budget deficits to three percent of gross domestic product as part of the qualification hurdles.

France's Socialist-led government announced extra taxes and savings last week to lop 0.4 percentage point off the budget deficit that was running at 3.5-3.7 percent of GDP. The Maastricht treaty says nations with deficits narrowing towards three percent can also qualify.
